title: Grounds for Refunding a Savings Account Fee, and the Courtesy Limits
content:
A fee posted to an account of Savings & Money Market Accounts is refunded on one of two grounds, and each ground carries its own conditions.

### Bank error

A bank error refund applies where the fee was assessed contrary to this charter — an excess withdrawal fee on a branch or ATM withdrawal, an excess withdrawal fee on a withdrawal within the free allowance, an excess withdrawal fee beyond the tier's cap on such fees in a cycle, or a maintenance fee in a cycle in which a waiver was met. A bank error refund has no time limit and does not count toward the courtesy limit.

### Courtesy waiver

A courtesy waiver refund of a correctly assessed fee is allowed only where every courtesy condition holds.

1. **Eligible fee code.** The fee must carry one of the courtesy-eligible fee codes: monthly maintenance, paper statement, excess withdrawal or dormant account.
2. **The rolling limit.** The customer's count of savings courtesy refunds in the rolling 365 calendar days ending on the current date must be below the courtesy refund limit of the tier, each refunded fee counting as one. The count is taken across all of that customer's savings accounts.
3. **Account status.** The account's status must be active or dormant when a courtesy refund is granted.
4. **Order of refunding.** Where the limit allows fewer refunds than are asked for, the most recently posted fees are refunded first, and among fees posted on the same day the larger fee is refunded first.
5. **Once only.** A fee can be refunded at most once.

Courtesy refunds on Personal Checking accounts and courtesy refunds on savings accounts are counted separately, so a checking courtesy refund never consumes the savings figure.

### Counting the courtesy refund window

The tier's courtesy refund window is counted in calendar days, with the day after the fee's posting date as day 1. A date falls within that window while it is on or before the fee's posting date plus the tier's courtesy refund window in calendar days; the comparison is not-later-than, so the last day of the window itself falls within it.

### No longer in force

Two clauses of this policy have been superseded and are not to be applied to any account of this product.

The clause that required a fee to be refunded in full and never in part, as a single refund entry whose source item was that one fee entry, is no longer in force.

The clause that required the fee itself to have posted no more than the tier's courtesy refund window in calendar days before the courtesy refund was granted is no longer in force. What remains in force is the counting of that window, set out above.

superseded_clauses: A fee is refunded in full, never in part, as one savings_fee_refund row whose source_item_id is the fee row.
The fee must have posted no more than courtesy_refund_window_days calendar days before the courtesy refund is granted.
